quotes.verbatim_quote:
Harmonic Major...a major scale with b6...(sometimes named Ionian b6.) Ail of the “red pages”
in Volumes 1 & 2 can be used with this very interesting variation: just play Ab (b6) instead of A (6).
There are nearly 200 pages to explore!
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the Harmonic Major (Ionian b6) scale and gives the practitioner a concrete substitution rule for applying it to existing material.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Hungarian Minor...a harmonic minor scale with #4..|C D E}FEG AbBC |. Allofthe "blue
pages" in Volumes 1 & 2 can be used with this amazing variation! There are nearly 200 pages to work with.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the Hungarian Minor scale with its characteristic #4 and directs the player to apply it across the existing volume's content.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
P.S. The IVLs and the FVLs are all examples of SCVL (specific chromatic voice-leading),
as opposed to GDVL (generic diatonic voice-leading), which is all of Volumes 1 & 2.

PPS. There, I gave it away!
quotes.why_load_bearing: Establishes the key conceptual distinction between specific chromatic voice-leading (used in the Grip-Slipping exercises) and the generic diatonic voice-leading of the prior volumes.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
"Grip-Slipping" is a term I use to describe a series of exercises that I sometimes give to
my guitar students to help them learn all the inversions of different chords. Without giving away
too many "secrets," I've included six examples incorporating seventh chords in a six tonic system
(whole tone scale). The voicing type is Drop 3. (You might try Drop 2 and Drop 2 & 4 as well...)
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the Grip-Slipping technique and its pedagogical purpose—learning all chord inversions—while specifying the voicing type and suggesting variations.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
I think it's clear that both writers are saying that melody has the edge over harmony. I would
disagree, but only slightly. I feel that excellent voice-leading treats both melody and harmony as
equals.
quotes.why_load_bearing: States the book's governing aesthetic rule: voice-leading excellence requires treating melody and harmony as equals, distinguishing this method from classical theory.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
I went back to my notes and DID THE MATH! Much to my surprise and delight, I realized
that I had completely overlooked SPREAD CLUSTERS! I did some more musical math and real-
ized that this was the missing link! It not only completed the set of 4-part chords, but it helped me
to realize that this WORK was not only finite, but do-able!
quotes.why_load_bearing: Identifies Spread Clusters as the chord family that completes the entire taxonomy of diatonic 4-part chords, making it the conceptual keystone of the system.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
We present it in 5 scales:

1. C Major

2. C Melodic Minor

3. C Harmonic Minor

4. C Harmonic Major (C Ionian b6)

5. C Hungarian Minor (C Harmonic Minor #4)

(Of course, this same approach could be applied to pretty much everything in all 3 volumes
by anyone interested...)
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the five-scale framework used in the M-Lode Plus section and explicitly invites the player to extend this approach to the full three-volume system.
